items.title: China’s Spies Set Sights on A.I. Chips Years Before Nvidia Scandal
items.summary: China’s espionage agency has been running a secret campaign to help the country’s companies acquire advanced A.I. chips and to gather intelligence on the sector, officials say.

items.title: Drones, Texts and Diversions: How Mexico Captured a Most Wanted Man
items.summary: U.S. and Mexican authorities shared intelligence for weeks to track Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, a drug cartel leader that a U.S. official called the most dangerous man in Mexico.

items.title: Who Is the Mexican Drug Kingpin Known as El Chapo Isidro?
items.summary: The kingpin, Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, was captured in a violent operation in Mexico. He was one of the F.B.I.’s 10 most wanted fugitives.

items.title: Tech Outages Are Only the Beginning. A.I. Will Bring More Disruptions.
items.summary: Cybersecurity has been an afterthought since the early days of the internet. Now A.I. is uncovering dormant problems, making the bill come due for decades of vulnerable code.

items.title: Trump Moves to Restrict Congressional Oversight of Contractors
items.summary: The president’s executive order is the latest effort to blunt Democratic plans to investigate the administration’s actions.

items.title: Jennifer Lopez Feels Like She’s Getting Better at Everything
items.summary: After a vulnerable and tumultuous run, the performer is back with a new TV spectacular and hard-earned boundaries.

items.title: Now Is Not the Time for Europe to Relax
items.summary: It’s easy to hope that our good old post-1945 Uncle Sam, holding his security umbrella over European and Asian allies, is back again. He isn’t.

items.title: The Sisterhood Rocks!
items.summary: But should daughters bear the brunt of their folks’ care?

items.title: Deadly Protests Erupt in Bangladesh Over Exiled Former Leader. What to Know.
items.summary: Supporters of the deposed prime minister, Sheikh Hasina, who was sentenced to death in absentia, have waged a small-scale insurgency to destabilize the current government.

items.title: Trump orders federal contractors to check with White House before responding to Congress
items.summary: President Trump is directing federal contractors to consult the White House about inquiries from Congress and to withhold any communications that his administration considers privileged.

items.title: Google employees protest AI in schools policy
items.summary: More than 550 Google employees signed a petition to allow schools access to Search without AI. Parents and educators protested outside Google offices in 6 cities last week for the same ask.

items.title: Highlights and challenges from covering an historic month in South America
items.summary: NPR's South America Correspondent discusses her work covering an historic election upset and a papal visit.

items.title: Bayer reaches Roundup settlement that could cost the company billions
items.summary: The money will go to thousands of people who have been or will be diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphoma – a blood cancer linked to the herbicide.

items.title: Storms expected on both coasts threatens Thanksgiving travel
items.summary: The mayor of San Francisco is asking people in the city not to travel unless "absolutely essential." Meanwhile, a storm moving up the Eastern seaboard could also cause travel delays ahead of Thanksgiving.

items.title: Cartel leader captured in northern Mexico in a bloody firefight that left 11 dead
items.summary: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, better known as "El Chapo Isidro," was one of the FBI's most wanted fugitives. His arrest in northwest Mexico on Saturday has sparked violence in the region.

items.title: Killer robots: U.N. talks fall short of hopes for legally binding rules
items.summary: U.N. talks in Geneva have failed to deliver binding rules on autonomous weapons, as humanitarian groups warn that military AI is advancing far faster than diplomacy.

items.title: Federal jury convicts man of starting the deadly 2025 Palisades Fire in Los Angeles
items.summary: Prosecutors argued the defendant, 30-year-old Jonathan Rinderknecht, had been "mad at everything" in the days leading up to the January 2025 fire, which killed 12 people.

items.title: Perspective: Defining 'human'
items.summary: The Cambridge Dictionary has chosen the word "human" as its Word of the Year. Why ever might a word that entered the English language over 500 years ago be so honored?

items.title: Senate permitting bill speeds up renewables, divides greens over oil and gas
items.summary: A permitting reform bill in the Senate could help speed the development of renewable energy projects, but it's splitting environmentalists over other provisions that help the oil and gas industry.

items.title: Was Trump’s news conference with Vance and Rubio an audition for 2028?
items.summary: Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are widely considered to be potential Republican presidential candidates.

items.title: Man convicted of starting deadly Palisades fire in California
items.summary: The Palisades fire destroyed more than 6,800 buildings across Los Angeles and Malibu, with officials estimating the damage bill at $25 billion.

items.title: Emergency medical services could be delivered by drones
items.summary: Pilot programs in the U.S. allow drones to transport medical items, which can include defibrillators, medicines or blood. Drone delivery of organs faces many hurdles.

items.title: A widower lost his wedding ring. A used-car sale brought it back to him.
items.summary: A Minnesota couple discovered the keepsake months later and set out to find its 85-year-old owner.

items.title: A fixture behind the plate for two teams and part of ‘baseball’s first family’
items.summary: Bob Boone endured the grueling physical toll of catching in the majors with remarkable toughness.

items.title: A stray puppy hopped onto a car salesman’s lap. It may have saved her life.
items.summary: When it turned out the dog was seriously ill, the family paid her $4,000 vet bill and adopted her.

items.title: Pandemic-era law passed unconstitutionally because of proxy voting, appeals court rules
items.summary: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the 5th Circuit upheld Texas’s injunction stopping accommodations for pregnant workers by targeting how Congress passed a massive Biden-era funding bill.

items.title: L.A. train heists net thieves more than $22 million in goods, feds say
items.summary: A Southern California crew is charged with breaking into more than 70 shipping containers in 31 months, stealing more than $22 million in shoes and other goods.

items.title: Federal health panel reshaped by RFK Jr. faces political interference concerns
items.summary: Some members of the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force expressed concerns that the changes from the Trump administration could make the group less reliable and more open to conflicts of interest.

items.title: U.S. stocks slump into correction territory amid tech and AI worries
items.summary: Markets on Friday posted their worst week since worries about President Donald Trump’s tariffs caused a global sell-off in April 2025.
